claims.text: Localized instrumented nanoindentation can capture mechanical heterogeneities in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Local mechanical heterogeneities in FeNiCrMn correlate with variations in microstructural features.
Combining nanoindentation with micro-scale tensile or compression testing provides a more detailed account of FeNiCrMn mechanical behavior than traditional bulk testing.
As-cast or recrystallized FeNiCrMn contains inherent microstructural variations.
Relevant microstructural heterogeneities include grain-size variation, phase distribution, and local defects.
Nanoindentation provides spatially resolved measurements of hardness and elastic modulus.
Nanoindentation hardness and elastic modulus reflect the local microstructural state of FeNiCrMn.
Micro-scale tensile or compression testing captures local stress-strain responses.
Combining the two methods allows local mechanical-property variations to be linked to overall deformation mechanisms.
Regions with higher nanoindentation hardness and modulus will exhibit increased local yield strength.
Regions with higher nanoindentation hardness and modulus will exhibit altered ductility.
The combined localized tests will reveal heterogeneous mechanical responses that are not observable in bulk tests.
Conventional bulk mechanical testing averages out local heterogeneities.
The proposed method is validated only under ambient-temperature, quasi-static conditions.
Applicability of the proposed method under high-strain-rate or high-temperature conditions is uncertain.
The quantitative relationship between nanoindentation measurements and micro-scale tensile or compression data is not fully established.
The magnitude of mechanical-property variation caused by microstructural heterogeneity is uncertain without further testing.
SEM can be used to examine alloy microstructures.
EBSD can characterize the microstructural features needed for correlation with localized mechanical measurements.
